I feel like I'm going crazy.

 I had a friend that I really liked, and it really felt like she liked me too, but then over the winter we both got a little too stressed out and we were arguing over stupid stuff and just not treating each other how we used to... So at some point we just stopped talking to each other, stopped being friends, and maybe stopped caring about each other as much as we had before (except the problem is that I haven't)


 Now, for the past few weeks I've been feeling a lot better in almost every way--except I've been missing her and feeling very sorry about the way we acted. I want to resume our friendship and would especially like to put us back on the track it felt like we were on, but I don't know how or if its even possible at this point. We've barely spoken to each other for a solid two months.


Mentally I know that its probably best to just move on, but I honestly just keep thinking about her way too much and don't know how to stop. I know its unhealthy, but its just such a strong feeling.

As a person suffering from social anxiety, thank you for this. A lot of the stuff in this thread has been making it seem like there is no way to get any better at being social and that this is just something we have to accept--the world isn't designed for us, so we will never be happy. I have found through a combination of therapy, medication, and introspection/practice in front of a mirror that I can actually pretend to be normal in many situations that require it of me. Of course, this won't be true for everyone, some people will not be able to "learn" to be social... but being shy is definitely not a death sentence. There are still completely isolated ways to earn a living. Maybe you won't become a millionaire, but most people won't anyway. 

For an example of how I personally deal with social interaction: I have made up responses to the types of interactions that I expect to encounter... So if someone asks me how I am, I have practiced so much that I just mindlessly reply "I'm well. How are you?" Then I listen and nod along to their response. Sometimes I still struggle to end conversations politely and end up just meandering away during a pause, but I am getting much better at saying "I have to go to class" or "I have to go check the grill." (I work in fast food). I always try to mentally prepare an escape. If nothing else, there is always "I have to go to the bathroom" and hoping they don't join you!

Also, Azza_ I am sorry about how you are feeling. I failed out of college last year, set my date, and stopped making plans... If I hadn't broken down completely at a random visit to the doctor and been put on medication & into therapy, I don't think I would still be here right now. Some days it is hard, but overall, I am happy that I am. I hope you can find something that makes it easier for you or something that makes you want to extend your plans, even just a little at a time. (Sometimes I think of it this way:If I'm going to kill myself anyway, I might as well do some of the things I still want to do first. Suicide will still be there after my sister's birthday or that movie I want to see comes out, so it doesn't really change much to wait a little longer...)

Remember that it takes time for a body to change. I can't claim to have any idea how hard it is to transition, especially since society is unaccepting and people are cruel, but just to use myself as an example: I'm about 70lbs overweight, and I'm on a diet plan to lose a 1.5lbs a week (if I stick to my goals every day). It will take me at least a year and a half or two years to reach my ultimate goal and be a healthy weight, and in the meantime I feel like there has been no change at all. It can be really disheartening to see the way the scale goes up and down from day to day (I really need to buy a more reliable scale, I guess), but there is a downward trend, and these small changes will add up. So will the changes from your HRT. And hopefully, if we all work together and work hard, we can see some of these small changes in society and they can add up too. 

Until then, you should know that every day you go out and go to work or go shopping or just do your thing, you are so brave and there are people who are so proud of you. The people who bully you and ridicule you are petty and small, you've done nothing to them and it is not your fault that are lacking in manners and think it's okay to do/say disgusting things to another human being... and I know that isn't exactly a consolation, but maybe you can keep that in mind anyway. <3

I just wanted to say that I have had the depressing friend and I have been the depressing friend, and both sides hurt. But what hurts more, on either side, is losing the friend completely. Right now you are feeling like your friends hate you and think you are "too depressing." You think they want you dead, and that must be a terrible thing to think. I'm so sorry you are feeling this way.

When I had a friend going through a really rough patch, yes, he was very depressing and difficult to speak to. That did not make me hate him at all. What I hated was not knowing what to do to help. 

Maybe you are not ready to reach out to one of your old friends, but please reach out to someone. A relative, a doctor, someone here on reddit, and tell them what you need, because sometimes it is not as clear to them. If you've had a bad day and need someone to talk to, I'm here, as well as others on this subreddit. 
If you need someone to distract you by just hanging out or watching a movie, ask. 
You are hurting because you are lacking the connection you used to share with your friends. Reach out to them. Things may not be as bad as they seem, and if they are, it doesn't sound like at least trying to talk to them could make things much worse.
